summary: Iteration 6 — verified the Twilio 'unverified caller ID' bug fixes end-to-end. Backend: 18/18 pytest GREEN in /app/backend/tests/backend_test_v6.py covering: (a) POST /leads/{id}/call with exec_phone=+15005550006 returns HTTP 400 with new actionable message 'Twilio rejected the call: the number +15005550006 is not a Verified Caller ID on this trial account. Add it at twilio.com/console/phone-numbers/verified, then retry. The lead's number must also be verified until you upgrade.' — the old cryptic 'Unable to create record' string is NOT present; (b) same 400 error-path triggered with an arbitrary unverified E.164 number (+919999999999) proving the parsing is number-agnostic; (c) empty exec_phone returns 400 with 'Set your phone (E.164, e.g. +9198…) on the Team page first' (matches frontend /Set your phone/i regex and includes E.164 hint for actionability); (d) /auth/refresh accepts a session with ONLY refresh_token cookie (access_token deleted), returns 200 and rotates a fresh access_token cookie; the replayed /auth/me then succeeds; (e) with BOTH cookies deleted, /auth/refresh → 401 and /auth/me → 401 (server does not loop); (f) enabling settings.auto_call_on_new_lead + creating a lead assigned to an executive whose phone is +15005550006 still returns 200 for POST /leads — the HTTPException raised by _initiate_twilio_call is caught (verified 'auto-call skipped:' warning appears in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log and no 500 is emitted); the lead persists (verified via GET); (g) regression: /users, /leads, /projects, /follow-ups, /site-visits, /twilio/status, /notifications, /admin/eod-summary, /dashboard/monthly, /dashboard/revenue-breakdown, /settings, /auth/me all 200 for admin. Frontend Playwright: (1) after logging in as admin, patched admin phone to +15005550006 → clicked [data-testid=lead-twilio-call-btn] on lead 170fe93… → toast text contained 'Twilio rejected the call' + '+15005550006' + 'Verified Caller ID' + 'twilio.com/console/phone-numbers/verified' AND the 'Update phone' sonner action button was present → clicking it navigated the tab to /team ✓. (2) With admin phone set to +919999999999 the toast surfaced the same new hint and echoed the new number (proving the LeadDetail.jsx regex /unverified|21219|Verified Caller ID/i catches any unverified number, not just the placeholder). (3) With admin phone set to '' the toast surfaced 'Set your phone (E.164, e.g. +9198…) on the Team page first' AND still offered the 'Update phone' action button. (4) Auth-refresh interceptor: after deleting only the access_token cookie via browser context.clear_cookies + add_cookies(non-access), navigating in-app to /leads triggered POST /auth/refresh (200) followed by a successful /auth/me (200); the tab stayed on /leads and was NOT redirected to /login. (5) Full-logout path: after clearing BOTH cookies, in-app navigation triggered one /auth/refresh attempt that failed 401, then Protected correctly booted to /login. No infinite loop observed (a single refresh attempt per request thanks to the `_retried` flag). Admin's original phone (+919606334692) was captured pre-test and restored in a session-scoped finalizer so seed state is preserved.

minor.issue: The 21219/'unverified' branch handles code=21219 and substring 'unverified'. Twilio's SDK also raises code=21214 ('to number cannot be reached') and 21210 ('from number invalid') for adjacent trial-mode failures — those still fall through to the generic 'Twilio error: {e}' path which is friendlier than before but not action-guided. Consider adding explicit branches for 21214/21210 with 'add the LEAD's number to Verified Caller IDs' hint since on a Twilio trial account both endpoints of the call must be verified.

Line 1527 has operator-precedence ambiguity: `if "21211" in msg or "invalid" in msg.lower() and "phone" in msg.lower():` — Python evaluates AND before OR, so this reads as `"21211" in msg  OR  ("invalid" AND "phone")`. That's probably intended but it's worth adding parens for readability, or a leading unit-test to lock the behavior.

phone field has no server-side E.164 validation. A user could store '12345' and only find out at call time. Consider a Pydantic validator (regex ^\+[1-9]\d{7,14}$) so the Team page returns 400 immediately rather than at call time.

issues: Recharts still logs 'width(-1) height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' warnings on initial render (carried from iteration 4/5) — cosmetic, doesn't affect functionality.

critical_code_review_comments: The axios interceptor de-dupes concurrent refreshes with `refreshInFlight` but ties the promise to the FIRST 401's config. If two independent 401s race, only one gets the retry — the other awaits the same refresh promise (via `refreshInFlight`) but then falls into the else branch that resolves it as a fresh in-flight call. This is subtle; consider a per-request queue that all pending 401s await, then each replays its own `original` config. Current code is correct for the common case but worth a test.

AuthContext.bootstrap() only calls /auth/me. If the very first /auth/me returns 401 during startup, the axios interceptor auto-refresh WILL fire and the retry will populate `user`. Good. But bootstrap() has no loading spinner state — user briefly sees `user=null` which Protected likely treats as 'loading'. Verify Protected explicitly distinguishes null (loading) vs false (logged out) which it appears to do based on the routing behavior observed.

server.py _initiate_twilio_call now correctly raises HTTPException(400) instead of 502 so the preview gateway does not rewrite JSON — good. But note: the auto-call path in create_lead (line 582) catches HTTPException and only logs .detail. If the lead's phone itself is invalid (raises HTTPException 400 'Lead has no valid E.164 phone'), we now swallow that as WARNING — arguably fine, but a lead created with an invalid phone will silently skip auto-call without notifying the creator. Consider surfacing a soft warning on the create-lead response body (`{lead, warnings: []}`) so the UI can toast.

LeadDetail.jsx call button uses `window.location.assign('/team')` inside the sonner action — this is a hard reload, losing SPA state. Prefer `navigate('/team')` via useNavigate() (already used elsewhere in the file). Cosmetic but consistent.
server.py is still 2627 lines. The Twilio block (~200 lines including callbacks) is another good router-split candidate along with the notifications/EOD blocks flagged in iteration 5.
TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER is exposed in backend/.env with real credentials — ok for preview but before production deploy, rotate the auth token and move to a secrets manager.

rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: /leads/{id}/call surfaced 'Twilio error: HTTP 400 error: Unable to create record' when the exec's stored phone was not a Verified Caller ID on the trial account (Twilio code 21219). Additionally, once the 12h access_token cookie expired, any axios call would 401 and Protected would boot the user to /login mid-workflow. Fix verified: (a) backend now catches 21219/'unverified' and returns a specific, actionable HTTP 400 that names the offending number and links the Twilio console; (b) axios interceptor now catches 401, POSTs /auth/refresh once, replays the original request, and only surfaces the 401 if refresh itself fails — with a `_retried` flag preventing loops and `refreshInFlight` de-duping concurrent refreshes; (c) LeadDetail.jsx toast now detects the new error via /unverified|21219|Verified Caller ID|Set your phone/i and offers an 'Update phone' action button that navigates to /team; (d) auto-call on lead-create swallows the new HTTPException so lead creation is never blocked. All four fix points reproduced and validated.
